column1: # source: tests/reference-frozen/java-head-2026-09/ (read ONCE, here, before the chmod -R a-w)
# timing: NONE, deliberately. Ruling BO forbids the jar as the timing reference -- a jar
#         cpu_s taken on one machine is a number with no meaning next to a port cpu_s, and
#         the frozen tree carries no timing anyway. The rolling PORT time baseline is
#         benchmark/baselines/stem-times.tsv and nothing here may stand in for it.
# WHAT THIS FILE IS. Numbers, quality only, context and NEVER a gate. It is the jar column
# scripts/quality-ab.sh renders into every row jar_incomplete, jar_violations,
# jar_clearance_violations and jar_normalized_score, so that a reader of one A/B row can
# see where the jar stood without opening a second file. No rule reads it, no flag comes
# from it, and it cannot change that script exit code. The gate is the PORT column,
# WHY IT LIVES HERE AND NOT IN THE FREEZE. BL8 as amended by ruling BP1: the frozen tree is
# a historical artefact, written once and read by nothing -- no test, no script. Deriving
# these numbers was the single, final read, and it happened before the tree was made
# read-only. grep -rn "reference-frozen" crates/ scripts/ benchmark/ returns prose only.
#       The REFEREE DRC document, never a manifest (survey 4.1: the manifest own counts
#       disagree with the program own -drc mode on 45-63% of boards, and several Plan 9
#       tasks are busy fixing exactly that). For the 8 batch and 13 CLI stems that is the
#       port -drc run over the JAR frozen SES -- the same instrument quality-ab.sh puts
#       the port own SES through, so the two columns are like for like and what differs
#       between them is the routed board and not the measurement. For the 8 DRC stems it
#       is the frozen drc-<stem>/drc.json itself, which IS the jar own document and is a
#       better jar number than re-refereeing the board with the port would be.
#       manifest.json, written by a second bare-jar run with --router.result_json.
#       These are board statistics and nothing disputes them.
#   the 8 DRC stems route nothing, so their routing columns read `-`. That is not a gap.
# THE BATCH ROWS SHARE THE CLI MANIFEST, and may do so. gen-cli-reference.sh asserts per
# stem that cli-<stem>/route.ses is byte-identical to <stem>/batch.ses, and Task 1
# re-verified it with cmp on all 8 before deriving anything. The manifest therefore
# describes the very board the batch row is about. The batch and cli rows for those 8
# stems are consequently identical, exactly as they are in the port own T0 column.
# THE ONE ROW WHERE THE JAR AND THE PORT DISAGREE, and it is a known one.
# drc/drc-natural-tone-preamp: jar 115 violations, port 112. Quirk #146, pinned by
# (DesignRulesChecker.java:271-276) and that phase dedup (:160) drops whichever dangling
# trace a net entry hash-ordered firstItem happens to be; the port ascending-id
# representatives make three more of them dangling. Every other one of the 29 rows matches
# the port T0 column exactly, which is what byte-parity at this commit means and is the
# reason this file is worth cutting at this commit and at no later one.
